newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ITALY TO WORK TO "LAST HOURS" ON ALBANIA POLL-PRODI.
newsitem.headline: ITALY TO WORK TO "LAST HOURS" ON ALBANIA POLL-PRODI.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Tuesday that Italy would work to the "last hours" to convince Albanian parties to hold elections, but Italy's presence would be reviewed if they did not agree.
"We are going to work until the last hours to see that the elections are ended before the summer holidays," Prodi said at a news conference in Hungary.

"The people in Albania understand there is no other choice for them and lately we have had intensive talks with their leaders and I demonstrated to them what a dramatic situation would arrive if elections were to be postponed," he added.

Italy, which leads a multinational troop force in Albania protecting aid supplies and maintaining order in some of the most lawless areas, has said it may pull out if the elections are not successful.
But Prodi denied a report that if there was no agreement by Monday that Italy would have to revise its Albania mission.
"What I said in Vienna was I warned that there was an extremely grave danger in the sense there is a strong internal disagreement in Albania that threatens external support," Prodi said.

"Unless there is an internal agreement concerning the elections our own mission will have to be revised once again because the first target of the mission was to reach as far as political elections which would be simple and transparent and just by that we could contribute to the rebirth of the country.
"Obviously if there is no internal agreement concerning the holding of elections it is necessary to revise the content of our mission in Albania," he added.
"But I must say that even in the very last hours the discussions...are to be continued and I do hope that we can reach the agreement we would like to have."

Prodi, who spoke at a news conference with Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, said the efforts to resolve the Albania crisis were an example of regional cooperation that the three leaders have sought to promote through a trialteral cooperation agreement.
Prodi said that as a result of such cooperative efforts "it seems that we will be able to avoid a Bosnia-type tragedy in the case of Albania".

Prodi made his remarks on the same day it was announced in Tirana that talks between Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and political parties had failed to produce agreement on ground rules for planned elections, which most parties are now threatening to boycott.
